clue: I carved a message into a coconut shell to help rescuers find my boat’s crew. Who am I?
explanation: John F. Kennedy used a coconut shell to send a rescue message after his patrol boat was wrecked. Islanders carried the message for help.

clue: I created the Peace Corps, a program for volunteers to help communities around the world. Who am I?
explanation: John F. Kennedy started the Peace Corps. Volunteers could help with teaching, farming, health care, and building projects.

clue: I was chosen to write the first draft of the Declaration of Independence. Who am I?
explanation: Thomas Jefferson drafted the Declaration of Independence in 1776. Other members of Congress also helped shape the final document.

clue: I designed my home on a mountain and named it Monticello. Who am I?
explanation: Thomas Jefferson designed Monticello. Enslaved people did the work of clearing the mountaintop where it would stand.

clue: I served as White House hostess during my father’s presidency in the winters of 1802–1803 and 1805–1806. Who am I?
explanation: Martha Jefferson Randolph helped host White House gatherings for her father, Thomas Jefferson. She was his daughter, not his wife.

clue: I helped my family gather and edit my father’s papers after his presidency. He was the third U.S. president. Who am I?
explanation: Martha Jefferson Randolph worked with family members to compile and edit Thomas Jefferson’s papers, helping preserve his writings.

clue: I ordered two cabinets to display dishes used by different presidential families. Who am I?
explanation: Edith Roosevelt commissioned cabinets for presidential china. These special dishes helped tell the history of the White House.

clue: I hired Isabella Hagner as the first White House social secretary. Who am I?
explanation: Edith Roosevelt hired Isabella Hagner to help organize letters, receptions, dinners, and other White House events.

clue: I turned the White House sun porch into a kindergarten for my daughter and other children. Who am I?
explanation: Jacqueline Kennedy made a classroom on the third-floor sun porch. Caroline and a small group of children came there for kindergarten.

clue: By age eleven, I had already won national horseback-riding championships. Later I became a first lady. Who am I?
explanation: Jacqueline Kennedy learned to ride as a very young child and won several national riding championships by age eleven.
